cases.notes: BeyondTrust bindiff: 'the one everyone is worried about seems to be in schannel!DecodeSigAndReverse'; new logic added in the middle of the function guarding two memcpy calls; other changed functions in DTLSCookieManager set aside by the author. Unit 42 (unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/code-trigger-ms14-066-ecdsa-server-bof-vulnerability/) names iCM_DecodeSigAndReverse for the vulnerable path but no patched function: naming contradiction, both accepted. Patched versions and KB from the cnblogs.com/LittleHann/p/4092058.html analysis (Chinese; summariser view). Old (2014) but fills the schannel gap.

cases.notes: K7: 'The vulnerable function Srv2DecompressData() has been patched in the srv2.sys driver' and shows RtlULongAdd in the patched code, but one figure caption says Srv2CompressionDecompress (internal inconsistency). Trellix/McAfee (trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/threat-labs/smbghost-analysis-of-cve-2020-0796.html) names Srv2DecompressData as vulnerable and describes RtlULongAdd/RtlULongSub in the fixed code but does not name a patched function. K7 links KB4541338; I could not confirm that is the security fix KB, so KB is deliberately not recorded. The earlier pass removed this CVE from windows-candidates.json for lack of a diff statement; K7 supplies one. srvnet.sys not named by either page.

Patch-Diffing-Applied table lists LcmCreatePortEntry as the changed function (new helpers IsValidNamedPipeOrCustomPort and IsPortNamedPipe). The same page quotes a public report saying the PortIsValid check was moved inside LcmXcvDataPort: contradiction, so both accepted. 0patch (0patch.com/blog/micropatching-printdemon-vulnerability) says Microsoft 'added a couple of checks in the code for creating a printer port', consistent with LcmCreatePortEntry; it names no function. May 2020 and KB4556799 (Win10 1909) from the cve-north-stars CVE page. Non-ZDI source.

Patch-Diffing-Applied lists five changed functions for this build pair (LcmCreatePortEntry, SplSetPrinterDataEx, PortIsValid, LcmStartDocPort, DoAddPort) plus new helpers IsMissingUNCPortsServicingEnabled, IsSpoolerImpersonating, IsValidSpoolDirectory. The page does not say which one is the security fix, so ground truth is a set, not a function: weak discriminating power, low confidence. Single source. Month not stated. Drop if a strict one-function case is required.

older.ref: vmswitch.sys, 2021-Apr (build needs pinning; Akamai says bug emerged in an Aug 2019 build)

cases.notes: 0vercl0k: 'The bug itself happens in VmsIfrInfoParams_OID_SWITCH_NIC_REQUEST'. Akamai (akamai.com/blog/security/critical-vulnerability-in-hyper-v-allowed-attackers-to-exploit-azure) lists the call chain RndisDevHostControlMessageWorkerRoutine, RndisDevHostHandleSetMessage, VmsIfrInfoParamsNdisOidRequestBuffer, VmsIfrInfoParams_OID_SWITCH_NIC_REQUEST and says vmswitch never validates OidRequest. Neither page says which function Microsoft changed, so this is the vulnerable function, not a confirmed diff result. Patch month May 2021 from both.

y3a says the vulnerable function is NtfsQueryEaUserEaList (no integer-underflow check), reached via NtfsCommonQueryEa. NCC Group (nccgroup.com/research/cve-2021-31956-exploiting-the-windows-kernel-ntfs-with-wnf-part-1/) names the same function and says patched in June 2021 Patch Tuesday. Neither page describes the code change or gives a KB/build. NtfsCommonQueryEa is the caller and is accepted only as a fallback.

0patch (summariser view): for CVE-2022-33647 Microsoft's original patch was in KerbInitPreferredCryptList (runs at KDC start); 0patch placed its own patch in KerbGetEncTypeBitmask. The 0patch micropatch post for 33647/33679 (0patch.com/blog/micropatches-for-kerberos-elevation-of) confirms kdcsvc.dll and Sept 2022 but names no function. So the function name is single-source. 6.1.7601.24499 on that page is the micropatch target, not a Microsoft pair. Companion CVE-2022-33679 not added (same fix, would double-count).

LOW TRUST. KernelSight (aggregator with auto-generated analysis, cites only the MSRC advisory) says 'the fix in KB5043076 adds explicit initialization of stack variables and heap buffers in GreGetGlyphOutlineInternal'. No independent source found. Binary label win32k.sys is as the source gives it; on Windows 11 the code may live in win32kfull.sys, so re-check which file actually changes before diffing. Month not stated. The only modern win32k case found with a named function that does not push win32kfull.sys past its cap.

Single source, aggregator of unknown authorship (same site as other cases flagged by the earlier pass); summariser view. Page: 32-bit 4*width*height wraps in SurfaceDecoderCpu::Init, fix widens to 64-bit and rejects zero/overflowed sizes, gated by Feature_2141685050, with a companion guard in CaCpuDecompressor (accepted as lower-ranked; the page does not give the exact symbol form).
